races.name: Betfair Backs Opinions Superior Mile Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Balmacara
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose recent form includes a third at 7f on soft ground, though jumping up to a mile on heavy is a clear stamina test; Eve Johnson Houghton's yard is 4/33 over 14 days and the 63-day absence is a minor flag, but similar-going record (9 runs, 1 win, 4 placed) suggests the ground is not an obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Balmacara shaped with promise when third four starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going to call on, but he arrives winless in his last five starts and a 63-day absence from stall three off 131 lb makes this a stern test.

runners_data.name: Dancing Gemini
runners_data.note: William Buick in the saddle is a significant upgrade for this hold-up horse whose flat form on good ground is modest, but the headgear flag (p) warrants monitoring; Roger Teal's 2/11 14-day record is quiet and 42 days off is not ideal — yet the horse's profile as a deep closer suits a race where the pace is honestly run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but Dancing Gemini's rating of 123 marks him as the one to beat here, and a return after 42 days off, experience over today's trip and going, and a weight of 131 lb from stall seven all set the stage for a bold bid.

runners_data.name: Fondo Blanco
runners_data.note: Ran just seven days ago, which is a fitness positive, and boasts two wins and five placings in similar soft/heavy conditions from 12 relevant runs; races prominently and will be fighting for a position that four others also seek, making traffic interference two furlongs out a real hazard.
runners_data.comment: Fondo Blanco showed he retains ability when runner-up last time out, and has run over today's trip, but two unplaced efforts in the runs before that and a ranking of seventh of nine on our figures make him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Consistent Group-level performer with a win and three places from six relevant soft-ground starts; James Doyle rides and races prominently, and the 14-day return is sharp — the concern is whether a horse that has done most of its best work over 9-10f truly sees out a mile as a test in heavy ground rather than as an advantage.
runners_data.comment: Persica steps out just 14 days after a winning effort two starts back, and his third last time out shows he retains form, with experience over today's trip and 118 on our figures marking him a clear threat; the concern is whether 131 lb from stall one ultimately stretches him.

runners_data.name: The Lost King
runners_data.note: His strongest credential is a win on soft and a placed effort in a Haydock similar-going context; PJ McDonald is an experienced partner and Andrew Balding's 8/53 14-day strike rate is workmanlike — races prominently and is among the most likely to secure that slot given his recent course-and-distance form at 8f.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins make The Lost King the one to beat here; he arrives on a sharp 16-day turnaround carrying a hefty 131 lb, and that weight could be the sole stumbling block to a hat-trick.

runners_data.name: Colori Forever
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying a 5lb age allowance and showing good 7-8f form on good ground, but only 1 run from 8 in similar-going conditions with no win — the heavy ground is a concern and racing prominently into a contested early pace may expose those limits.
runners_data.comment: Colori Forever brings solid recent form — a second last time out and a winner three starts back — though the unplaced effort two starts back and a 58-day absence are mild negatives to weigh against his distance-and-going experience and a rating of 109.

runners_data.name: Hankelow
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with one heavy-ground run in his five-race history (finished third at 8f on heavy, which is directly relevant); K.R. Burke sends out 10/39 over 14 days and the 14-day return is fine — will battle Needle Match for the lead and whether he can sustain the gallop in energy-sapping conditions is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Hankelow finished ninth and unplaced in his last two starts, and at a rating of 104 ranked eighth of nine runners he faces a stiff ask here; a third three starts back and a win four starts back offer some encouragement, and he has run over today's trip before, but recent form makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Needle Match
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old front-runner whose best form is a win on soft and a placing at 6f; only 4 runs in similar going with one win, and the step up from 6-8f to 8f on heavy ground requires stamina reserves that are genuinely uncertain — the 30-day break is neutral.
runners_data.comment: Needle Match showed up with a win four starts back and a placed effort last time out, but two disappointing runs in between temper expectations; he has experience over today's trip and returns after 30 days off carrying 126 lb from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Redemption Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with multiple third-place finishes suggesting consistent but limited form; Michael Keady has 0 wins from 11 runners over 14 days and the 86-day layoff is the most significant concern in the field — did well to place twice on soft in recent history but needs everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: Redemption Road has been winless in his last five starts, with three thirds offset by a pair of disappointing efforts, and 86 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, but ranked bottom of nine on our figures, he is hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Hankelow and Needle Match are the two confirmed pace-setters and will contest the lead from the off over this flat Haydock mile on heavy ground, creating a genuinely contested early tempo rather than an uncontested dawdle. Four of the nine runners — Fondo Blanco, Persica, The Lost King, and Colori Forever — all want to race prominently, meaning there will be significant pressure and potential crowding for position between two and three furlongs out as the heavy ground saps energy and the field begins to compress. The front two are unlikely to be able to stretch clear with that volume of horses pressing into them, which should produce a strong, honest gallop that turns this into a stamina and staying-power test over the final two furlongs. This race shape favours hold-up horses with proven ability to pick up off a genuine pace on soft or heavy ground — particularly those with the class and jockey craft to navigate what will be a congested stretch run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hankelow and Needle Match set a genuine contested gallop and the prominent group burn each other out approaching the straight.
scenarios.body: The heavy ground and pressure from four prominent horses ensures the pace is honest throughout, leaving closers with a strong enough tempo to aim at in the final two furlongs; hold-up runners who can produce a sustained finish are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent trio — Persica or The Lost King — settles just behind the pace-setters and benefits from a split or first run at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: On heavy ground a horse who races in the slipstream of the pace and picks up early can hold on as the hold-up horses are still weaving through traffic; The Lost King's recent heavy-ground win and Persica's consistent Group-level placing record make both credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If the early contest between Hankelow and Needle Match is fierce enough that both front-runners capitulate before the two-furlong pole, creating a vacuum.
scenarios.body: A strung-out field on heavy ground with a collapsed pace can paradoxically reward the deepest closers if there is still enough early tempo to have exposed weaknesses in the prominent brigade; Dancing Gemini with William Buick would be primed for a late surge in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Hankelow or Needle Match establishes a clear break early while the other fades or fails to press, leaving an uncontested lead on slow ground.
scenarios.body: Heavy ground occasionally allows a lone front-runner to slow the pace to a crawl and win with a controlled display, but with four prominent horses likely to push up and challenge, this outcome is the least probable; Needle Match's Haggas stable form makes it the most plausible candidate if a clear lead emerges.

watchPoints.text: Fondo Blanco, Persica, The Lost King and Colori Forever all want prominent ground simultaneously — expect fierce jostling for position between 1f-3f out, creating a genuine interference risk that could unsettle any of them.

Hankelow and Needle Match will press each other hard for the lead on energy-sapping heavy ground — watch whether either capitulates before the home straight, which would dramatically restructure the race shape mid-running.

Dancing Gemini's headgear (p, presumably a hood or similar) is new or notable — if it fails to sharpen the horse's early focus, the hold-up plan could leave William Buick with too much to do from off a heavy-ground pace.

Redemption Road's 86-day absence for a three-year-old with Michael Keady's quiet recent strike rate (0/11 over 14 days) makes this runner a watch for a race-rusty performance — its hold-up style means it needs everything to go perfectly and a smooth passage through traffic.

The Lost King's single heavy-ground run from 13 similar-going starts (1 win, 1 placed) is a thin record for the conditions — despite recent good form, monitor whether he handles the energy drain of true heavy ground when asked to race prominently throughout.

races.name: Betfair Celebrates Bow Echo Ascendant Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Arthurian
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's colt showed fair form (2nd, 6th) on Good ground at shorter trips and has genuine pace, but with First Law and Rocket Boy equally keen for the front, he faces a fierce battle for position that could cost him dearly in the energy-sapping heavy ground before the race even begins in earnest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked fifth of six on our figures, Arthurian faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip before and a second last time out offers a crumb of form; the 130 lb burden adds to his burden.

runners_data.name: First Law
runners_data.note: The class act on form figures — sole winner in the field, successful over this exact mile trip at Goodwood — with William Buick a major asset for controlling pace, though the step up to genuine heavy ground from Good is an unproven variable that represents his key question mark.
runners_data.comment: First Law won last time out, which is the chief point in his favour, but ranked last of six on our figures and carrying 130 lb from stall 3, he faces a stiff task against superior-rated rivals on what is a thin profile.

runners_data.name: Rafe's Da Man
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's progressive colt has been running into form (1st at Goodwood 7f, Good) and his prominent style means he will sit just off the pace war without being embroiled in it, which is structurally ideal for a heavy-ground stamina test; Levey's T14 record of 1/52 for Hannon is modest but the horse's own trajectory is the stronger signal.
runners_data.comment: Rafe's Da Man arrives here in good heart following his win last time out, and he has experience over today's trip to call upon, carrying 130 lb from stall six. The significant concern is a trainer currently without a winner in 45 runners over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Rocket Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good and placed over a mile on Good, so the trip extension is not a concern, but Marco Botti's colt will need to burn early energy fighting First Law and Arthurian for the front, making it hard to see how he sustains that effort across a mile of heavy Haydock turf in a Listed-class field.
runners_data.comment: Ran third last time out after winning two starts back, and Rocket Boy arrives here in decent nick on 24 days' rest, with experience over today's trip and carrying 130 lb from stall five. The one to beat.

runners_data.name: Romanza
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' filly brings the widest recent form profile — she has placed on Soft at Sandown and over a mile on Good — and her prominent style keeps her out of the front-running melee while still tracking the race; at OR 85 she has the most to find on ratings but her versatility on varying ground is a genuine asset in this conditions-driven race.
runners_data.comment: Romanza has been knocking on the door, finishing third last time out and second two starts back, and his consistent profile is backed by a rating of 92 in a field of six; yet to win in his last four starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Theheatison
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's hold-up specialist has winning form on Firm and placed on Soft, giving her a broad going tolerance, and her recent return just 16 days ago is the freshest prep in the field; the concern is that her natural hold-up style over a mile — the shortest trip at which she has run — leaves her needing a truly extreme pace collapse to get competitive in time.
runners_data.comment: Theheatison arrives in good heart after a runner-up finish last time out and a win four starts back, and he has run over today's trip before — a solid profile that makes him a genuine danger. The main risk is whether 130 lb will blunt his finishing effort.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — First Law, Arthurian, and Rocket Boy — will contest the lead immediately from the gates on Haydock's testing heavy ground over a mile, guaranteeing a relentless, contested gallop from the outset. William Buick on the Appleby-trained First Law (the sole winner in the field at this trip) and Marco Ghiani on Rocket Boy will be most aggressive for the rail position, with Arthurian likely to be pushed into an awkward middle-ground if he cannot assert early enough. The resulting strong pace on gruelling heavy ground will stretch the field across Haydock's flat mile, sucking the speed out of the lead contestants and turning this into a profound stamina examination in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners with proven heavy-ground durability who can settle off the suicidal pace and finish powerfully — horses like Rafe's Da Man and Romanza, who sit just off the action, are structurally well-placed, while Theheatison's hold-up style could see it benefit most of all if it can get competitive in time.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Burn Out
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle between First Law, Rocket Boy, and Arthurian produces an honest-to-brutal gallop that exhausts all three in the testing heavy ground.
scenarios.body: The lead trio set a punishing tempo that drains their stamina reserves well before the final furlong, leaving the race open to those who settled off the pace; prominent runners Rafe's Da Man and Romanza, having tracked the carnage from a comfortable position, are best placed to collec the spoils.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: First Law Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If William Buick times the pace perfectly on First Law, stealing a march without over-exerting, and the others fail to properly challenge him for the lead.
scenarios.body: First Law's sole listed win came over this exact trip on good ground, and Buick's race-reading ability could allow him to dictate at a sustainable tempo even on heavy going, denying rivals a target-rich finish; with Appleby's yard in reasonable form, this is the scenario where class and jockeyship trump the pace scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so extreme and the heavy ground so draining that even the prominent racers are weakened, leaving a gap for Theheatison to close from the rear.
scenarios.body: Theheatison has won on Firm and placed on Soft, giving it the widest going profile in the field, and a truly suicidal pace could create enough daylight for Stevie Donohoe to reel in the exhausted leaders; the risk is covering enough ground in time from a hold-up position over just a mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Slowdown Suits Romanza
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners nullify each other early but then ease the tempo, turning this into a more tactical affair that rewards a horse with a genuine finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Romanza has placed at 7f on Soft at Sandown and shown ability to quicken from a prominent pitch, and a steadier early pace on heavy ground could allow her to use that ability rather than simply grind; however, her lower OR of 85 makes this scenario genuinely unlikely against stronger rivals.

watchPoints.text: Watch First Law and Rocket Boy at the break — if both jump sharply and contest the lead aggressively, the pace will be genuinely brutal and neither is likely to see out the mile on heavy ground in prime condition.

Monitor Arthurian's early positioning: if he cannot assert and is pushed into the pack, his prominent-style energy is wasted and he may be compromised before halfway, effectively removing him from contention.

Rafe's Da Man's jockey Sean Levey must resist any temptation to go with the pace — if he settles cleanly just off the leaders, the horse's recent winning form and suited prominent style make him the primary beneficiary of the expected pace collapse.

Theheatison's hold-up profile is the hardest to execute over just a mile on heavy ground — watch whether Donohoe chooses to ride her closer than usual, as a position change could materially alter her chance in the closing stages.

The going is described as Heavy across all races on the card, with no differentiation — any horse that has previously shown a marked preference for better ground, particularly Arthurian and Rocket Boy whose form is exclusively on Good, faces a significant and unquantified test of adaptability today.

races.name: Best Odds On The Betfair Exchange Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Galilean Quality
runners_data.note: Has won at 1m4f on good-to-soft and soft, but this heavy ground at 1m6f is a stern stamina test; sole confirmed front-runner who should enjoy a freehold on the lead, though the style-fit flag suggests this P role is slightly out of character and the extended trip on extreme going introduces genuine stamina doubt.
runners_data.comment: Galilean Quality arrives on the back of a win two starts ago and has been placed last time out, showing he is in fine fettle just 14 days on; he has run over today's trip and, carrying 135 lb, his consistency across recent starts makes him the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bay
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding three-year-old with wins at 1m4f on both soft and good-to-soft, progressive profile and a proven prominent style — Daniel Tudhope's positional awareness is an asset, and the class edge (OR 92) over most rivals makes him the most dangerous immediate pursuer of the leader.
runners_data.comment: Mythical Bay arrives in fine nick, a winner two starts back and boasting three wins in his last six starts, with experience over today's trip and a lively rating of 97 backing his claims — the ninth last time out is the one blot that must be explained.

runners_data.name: Pierre Grosse
runners_data.note: Trained in Ireland by Mrs John Harrington, last ran 28 days ago and showed a 2nd at 1m5f on soft in his recent history, giving him the most relevant similar-going evidence in the field; rides with a 5lb claim via Kennedy and his natural hold-up style means he must hope the pace is genuine enough to bring him into it.
runners_data.comment: Pierre Grosse has placed twice in his last three starts but that elusive win continues to escape him, and while he has a solid profile of consistency and goes into this fresh enough after 28 days off, carrying 123 lb on a mark of 84 may prove a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Asia Force
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on this K.R. Burke-trained three-year-old who won last time over 1m4f on good; a true hold-up horse in nature, the redistribution into midfield means Buick may need to push earlier than ideal — his single similar-going run produced a third, and the style displacement tempers expectations regardless of his class.
runners_data.comment: Asia Force won last time out and has run over today's trip, but ranked sixth of eight on our ratings, he faces a stiff task confirming that form counts for enough here, despite the 122 lb burden looking manageable on an official mark of 83.

runners_data.name: Lopeo
runners_data.note: David Menuisier runner last seen 63 days ago, with a win on heavy at 8f back in his form string and two placing efforts at 1m4f-1m6f on good — the layoff and step up in ground are both relevant flags, but the heavy-going win provides genuine evidence others lack and his hold-up style is authentic rather than redistributed.
runners_data.comment: Lopeo showed smart form with back-to-back seconds before a seventh last time out, and has experience over today's trip and conditions carrying 122 lb; our rating of 91 marks him as a leading threat, though that 63-day absence is the one factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Reem Rak
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's charge holds a 1m4f win on good and a second on soft, but is a true hold-up type forced into a midfield mapping that is not his natural ground; Ray Dawson rides, and with OR 80 this horse needs a truly run race on testing ground to get competitive — the style displacement is a meaningful handicap here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Reem Rak faces a stiff ask, though she arrives in fair nick — third last time out, and a winner two starts back — and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Bridge Of Eagles
runners_data.note: Second Menuisier runner, also absent 63 days and stepping up significantly in trip from a 1m2f profile — won at 1m2f on good, but has only thirds at 1m2f on good in similar-going efforts and the stamina for 1m6f on heavy is a legitimate concern; prominent style is genuine and maps well, but the distance question is real.
runners_data.comment: Bridge Of Eagles shaped with plenty of credit when third last time out and, rated 87 by our assessors, has the quality to pose a serious threat here; the main risk is a 63-day absence on his return.

runners_data.name: Cotton Bud
runners_data.note: Shaun Lycett's charge is a naturally prominent type that the race shape cannot accommodate at the front, so sits in a midfield map that does not reflect his instincts; last ran 35 days ago, OR 72 is lowest in field, and on heavy ground over 1m6f the combination of trip, weight-adjusted rating, and a racing position he will not naturally settle into makes this a difficult task.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the field on our figures, Cotton Bud has failed to hit the frame in her last two starts and faces a stiff ask here, though she does have experience over today's trip and a win three starts back offers some encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Galilean Quality is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish over 1m6f on heavy ground at Haydock. Mythical Bay and Bridge Of Eagles are the natural prominent types best placed to track Galilean Quality through the early and middle stages, giving them the clearest sight of the race. The heavy going over this distance will stretch the field into a strung-out procession, ruthlessly exposing any horse low on stamina reserves or forced to race wide and exposed. This shape strongly favours horses who can be covered up just behind the lead and stay on relentlessly through the gruelling conditions — stalking types who settle early and grind late are the primary beneficiaries; it must also be noted that this field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can all secure their natural position, with Cotton Bud, Asia Force, and Reem Rak all likely to be squeezed into unfamiliar ground and denied their optimal racing patterns.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Galilean Quality Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Galilean Quality finds an uncontested lead and sets a measured, stamina-sapping tempo on the heavy.
scenarios.body: Galilean Quality bowls along in front at a pace that suits this ground, with the race effectively run to his rhythm, exhausting closers who must work harder through the deep going to close; prominent stalkers immediately behind him get the clearest run and are first to capitalise if he weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Galilean Quality's lead is tracked closely by Mythical Bay or Bridge Of Eagles who have enough left to overhaul him in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The pace set by Galilean Quality on heavy ground over 1m6f is sufficient to ensure he cannot sprint clear late, and a horse tucked in second or third all along swoops as the leader's stamina is tested in the final climb; this suits front-end horses with proven staying credentials and a jockey who times the challenge correctly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Aids Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is strong enough throughout to genuinely burn off all the prominent horses, leaving a genuine long-range stayer to come from further back.
scenarios.body: Heavy ground over 1m6f at a genuine pace can occasionally see the prominent horses all stop together in the straight, opening a late window for a horse tracking midfield with a true stamina profile; Pierre Grosse and Lopeo, both holding heavy-ground form and staying pedigree, are the ones most likely to capitalise in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion of hold-up types forced out of their natural position disrupts the race shape entirely, causing scrimmaging early and a messy, uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: Cotton Bud, Asia Force, and Reem Rak, none racing in their true position, create interference through the early stages as runners jockey for spots they cannot all hold, producing an uneven pace that scrambles the expected race pattern; in this muddled scenario a lightly weighted, adaptable horse who copes wherever they settle is most likely to benefit.

watchPoints.text: Galilean Quality's stamina on true heavy ground over 1m6f is the key variable — if he weakens sharply inside the final two furlongs after setting an uncontested pace, the entire race shape collapses and the beneficiary is whoever has tracked him most closely.

Cotton Bud, Asia Force, and Reem Rak are all likely to be jostling for positions that do not match their natural style in the early stages — watch for crowding or interference between the 1m and 1m2f marks as these horses try to find a comfortable berth.

Bridge Of Eagles and Lopeo have both been absent 63 days for Menuisier — a stable that has returned 0 wins from 20 runners in the past 14 days; a workout or market move in the final hour is worth monitoring given the dual runners after a long break.

Lopeo's heavy-ground win is the most specific going evidence in the field for this condition — if the ground is testing enough to make others struggle, his stamina credentials over the trip become materially more relevant than his current OR suggests.

Daniel Tudhope on Mythical Bay is the standout jockey booking in the race and the Andrew Balding yard is 8 from 53 over 14 days — a live combination whose positive trainer metrics in the short window are worth factoring into the prominent-stalker scenario.

races.name: Betfair Exchange Old Borough Cup Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Aegean Prince
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's four-year-old carries top weight for a yard in excellent recent form (T14: 4/12) and has two wins from four starts on similar going; returning from 320 days off is the key risk, but sim-going form of 2W2P and a prominent style right behind the lone leader puts him in an ideal tactical position if fully fit.
runners_data.comment: Aegean Prince arrives on the back of two wins in his last four starts, including a victory two starts back, and his 138 lb burden underlines his class — though the 320-day absence is the one factor to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Stressfree
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with poor recent form (6th, 8th, 11th in last three) and zero wins or places from 15 starts on similar going — the Heavy surface is no excuse given this record; Mark Winn rides for O'Meara's large but currently below-par string, and this horse needs a truly run race that the pace map suggests will not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Stressfree nevertheless shapes as the one to beat on our rating, and a second five starts back hints at the ability to land this off 136 lb, with experience over today's distance and going an added positive.

runners_data.name: Valedictory
runners_data.note: Gosden-trained four-year-old with two wins in recent form over 14f, though all his best efforts have come on Good ground; blinkers fitted, prominent style suits the race shape, but a step up to Heavy going is an unproven variable that James Doyle will need to manage carefully from a prominent pitch.

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: Won over this 16f trip on Good and has soft-ground experience, but the two sim-going starts produced just one place from fifteen and he ran poorly last time (ninth of fifteen on Soft); Ian Williams' yard is modest in the T14 stat and David Egan will need to thread through a busy prominent group from what may become an awkward berth.
runners_data.comment: Dancing In Paris bounced back to winning form last time out and has run over today's trip, but a patchy recent record — a fifth and unplaced efforts before that win — suggests consistency remains an issue, and 132 lb is no easy burden.

runners_data.name: In The Breeze
runners_data.note: Henrietta Knight's eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up type with four wins on Soft going, but his best form has been on Standard and Good, and his last six sim-going runs have produced only one finish in the top half; needs the pace to collapse to close, which this race shape is unlikely to deliver.
runners_data.comment: In The Breeze won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, returning fit on 17 days' rest and carrying 131 lb off an official mark of 92; the main risk is that he was unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: Mountain Road
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's seven-year-old has finished first, second or third in five of his last six and all recent runs have been over this 16f trip on Good; no sim-going data is a mild concern on Heavy, but Paul Mulrennan keeps the horse handy, the yard's T14 stat is fair and his form profile is the most consistently solid in the prominent pack.

runners_data.name: Finalise
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lone front-runner gets a dream scenario: unchallenged lead, no pace rival, and the ability to control fractions on testing ground; sim-going record of 0W2P over shorter distances is a slight note, but as the only horse guaranteed its preferred position, the tactical advantage is very significant.
runners_data.comment: Finalise arrives here in solid recent form, placed in all five of her last five starts with a win three starts back, and she handles today's trip with 27 days between runs suggesting she arrives fresh; the concern is whether she can convert her consistency into victory under 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Synergism
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's four-year-old won over 14f on Good and has consistent prominent form; the hood is fitted and the trainer's record of patient placement makes this interesting, but zero wins from four starts on similar going and a step into Heavy is a material step up in test — Marco Ghiani will need to navigate a congested middle pack.

runners_data.name: Ashnak
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win on Soft and two places from nine sim-going starts; David O'Meara's yard has a massive string (T14: 7/48) and Tudhope keeps him in the firing line, but a record of 7th, 2nd, 4th, 3rd, 8th in recent outings shows a horse who gets close without always delivering.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ashnak does show a second two starts back alongside a third four starts back, hinting at ability, but he returns after 42 days off and his speed rating of 81 leaves him with ground to make up from sixth in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Comfortably the horse most compressed by the pace map — a natural prominent racer who will find the six-horse scrum ahead of him makes his favoured berth unavailable, effectively relegating him to midfield with his style undermined; Charlie Johnston's yard has had some T14 success, but the OR of 83 and a style-fit discount of 0.94 both temper expectations sharply.
runners_data.comment: Pole Star has been placed third last time out but is winless in his last six starts, with a ninth three starts back among the low points; he has run over today's trip and comes here fresh enough on 20 days' rest, though a rating of 93 suggests he retains ability to make his presence felt from the middle of the field.

runners_data.name: Hermetic
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' four-year-old has placed four times at 16f but only on Good or better going; his natural prominent racing style will be squeezed out by the traffic in front, meaning he races in an uncomfortable midfield role throughout, and a career record of 0 wins from four sim-going starts does nothing to suggest Heavy ground unlocks him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Hermetic has been frustratingly consistent in all the wrong ways, rarely threatening beyond a string of fourths, and our rating of 88 ranks him ninth of eleven here — making him hard to fancy at this level despite carrying a manageable 120 lb fresh from a 28-day break.

runners_data.name: Glen To Glen
runners_data.note: Headgear-fitted hold-up horse who won over 20f on Good at his best — the stamina base is genuine, but the switch to Heavy going is untested in the recent record, and the trainer (Nick Scholfield, T14: 3/16) is a modest yard for this grade; Stevie Donohoe will need chaos ahead of him to deliver.

runners_data.name: Kissmehoneyhoney
runners_data.note: Haggas's second runner has a compact form record of just three runs, including a win on Soft and a place on Good; naturally wants to race prominently but will be physically unable to reach that position given the congestion — Sean Bowen will be managing a horse racing against its instincts in midfield, and the OR of 79 is a significant class concession to the principals.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into second last time out, which is a positive, but that eighth two starts back is a concern, and she ranks tenth of eleven on our figures — hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Golden West
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old is a hold-up type with two second-place finishes but zero wins from eleven sim-going starts; Duran Fentiman rides a horse who needs others to find trouble ahead and whose form figures 8, 9, 2, 4, 8 on similar ground paint a consistent picture of moderate reliability without a winning moment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Golden West is hard to fancy despite carrying a workable 117 lb fresh from a 29-day break; his two second-place finishes — most recently last time out and again three starts back — show he can hit the frame, but that is the kindest case here.

races.paceDynamic: Finalise is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead, Tom Marquand can dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop on testing Heavy ground — a significant tactical advantage over 1m6f at Haydock. Behind him, a congested prominent group of Aegean Prince, Valedictory, Dancing In Paris, Mountain Road, Synergism and Ashnak will jostle for the four or five positions immediately off the pace, creating compression and traffic danger from the home turn to the two-furlong pole. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Pole Star, Hermetic and Kissmehoneyhoney are genuine prominent racers who are unlikely to secure that territory and will effectively be racing in midfield against their natural instincts. On Heavy ground over an extended trip with a sole, unchallenged pace-setter controlling fractions, this race shape strongly favours proven front-runners and horses that can be ridden prominently with cover, particularly those with a confirmed stamina base and soft-ground form — late closers who need a truly-run test to close the gap will find a sustainable, compressed gallop working against them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Finalise Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Finalise is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a steady but sapping Heavy-ground tempo that sucks the life from the prominent pack.
scenarios.body: Marquand dictates on a horse proven to front-run and stay, and the energy expended by six prominent types scrapping for position behind depletes their reserves on testing ground; Finalise's supreme positional comfort on this surface makes him very hard to peg back in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace set by Finalise allows one or two of the well-placed prominent horses to cruise upsides entering the straight and collar the leader on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Aegean Prince or Mountain Road, each with strong Heavy/Soft form and proven stamina, can sit close enough behind Finalise to benefit from the lead without burning energy in the midfield scrimmage; both have the class and form profile to outstay the front-runner if he has given too much.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle creates an unusually fierce early pace that genuinely burns off the leaders and leaves a clear late-run opportunity.
scenarios.body: In The Breeze and Stressfree are the truest hold-up runners here with genuine come-from-behind profiles, and heavy ground tests stamina enough that a collapse in the lead could theoretically open a late lane; however, the pace map suggests a controlled rather than a genuinely scorching gallop, making this the less likely delivery.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Delivers Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If early prominent congestion causes traffic incidents, interference or a bunched finish that randomises the outcome.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of Pole Star, Hermetic and Kissmehoneyhoney into midfield means they are racing against their instincts and may attempt to push forward, causing interference between the two-mile marker and the home turn; in a chaotic finish on Heavy going Glen To Glen, who won over extreme distances on Good and has headgear fitted, or Golden West could sneak into contention from the back.

watchPoints.text: Finalise holds a unique structural advantage as the only unchallenged front-runner — watch whether Marquand elects to exploit this immediately or is instructed to conserve energy, as the tactical decision in the first half-mile will define the shape of the entire race.

Six prominent-profile horses (Aegean Prince, Valedictory, Dancing In Paris, Mountain Road, Synergism, Ashnak) are converging on the same three or four positions behind the leader — watch for bumping and interference between the 10f mark and the home turn where the track narrows.

Pole Star, Hermetic and Kissmehoneyhoney may all attempt to push forward from their mapped midfield positions to reclaim their natural prominent territory — if two or three simultaneously attempt this move between the 12f and 10f marks, the collision risk for those tracking the pace escalates sharply.

In The Breeze won over this course and distance on Soft going and has four career wins on testing surfaces — if the prominent battle is messier and more energy-sapping than the pace map anticipates, watch whether Ray Dawson has manoeuvred into a clear outer lane by the two-furlong pole.

Mountain Road's recent record of placing consistently over 16f at Haydock and Goodwood, combined with Paul Mulrennan's ability to secure a prominent position early, makes him the horse most likely to emerge cleanly from the prominent group if the scrimmage behind Finalise produces casualties.

races.name: Betfair Sprint Cup Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almeraq
runners_data.note: Unbeaten front-runner trained by William Haggas with three recent wins over this course and distance on good to soft; heavy ground is an unknown — his sim-going record of 3W from 8 runs is solid but none clearly on heavy — and 56 days off the track adds minor freshness doubt, though Tom Marquand is a strong booking and the horse sets the pace regardless.|
runners_data.comment: Almeraq has won three times in his last five starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, and has experience over today's trip; carrying 131 lb after a 56-day absence is the one thing punters must weigh up.

runners_data.name: American Affair
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's tough six-year-old arrives just 15 days since his last run and has won over five furlongs on soft, suggesting he stays well enough in testing conditions; he wants to be prominent but faces a wall of natural leaders and may be shuffled back, with his best chance coming if stamina becomes the premium.|

runners_data.name: Aramram
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old has a genuine win over six furlongs on soft and a solid recent form line including a course win, but his natural race position is prominent — a spot that is already oversubscribed here — meaning he is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal, which tempers confidence in a forward result.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures, Aramram has won once in his last five starts, with a fifth last time out doing little to encourage, though he has experience over today's distance and going and returns after a twenty-one day break carrying 131 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Big Mojo
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on Michael Appleby's four-year-old, who landed a six-furlong win on good going at Goodwood but whose heavy-ground form is thin (0 from 15 in similar going); wants a prominent pitch which will be fiercely contested, so Buick's tactical intelligence becomes crucial.|
runners_data.comment: Big Mojo arrives here in fine heart off a 27-day break, a winner last time out and carrying the fitness of a horse in form, with experience over today's trip and a solid rating of 117 backing his claims; the main risk is that his form in the four starts prior to that victory was notably weak.

runners_data.name: James's Delight
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's five-year-old has placed twice from 15 runs in similar going conditions and his best form has come in a prominent role; placed here at hold-up purely because the prominent positions are oversaturated, and racing from the rear is against his instincts, making it hard to have full confidence in a late flourish.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, James's Delight faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and arrives in fair nick 27 days on from a placing.

runners_data.name: Kind Of Blue
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's five-year-old returns after 77 days off but has multiple placed efforts over six furlongs on good ground with James Doyle in the saddle; genuine heavy-ground form is limited, and the long break is a concern, though a prominent style means he could track the leaders and benefit if they tire.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent when in the mood but winless in recent starts, Kind Of Blue shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back and third five starts back; he has run over today's trip and, rated 118, looks the one to beat if bouncing back after 77 days off.

runners_data.name: Marvelman
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old is a confirmed front-runner who has placed four times in his last five starts, including two runs on soft; notably, his recent form has come over seven furlongs and his only heavy-ground experience is sparse, raising questions about whether he can match Almeraq and Coppull's gate speed over the shorter trip.|
runners_data.comment: Marvelman shapes as a leading threat here, returning on a quick 14-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going, and his two most recent outings include a third last time out and a second three starts back; the main risk is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Paborus
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's five-year-old arrives on the back of a six-furlong win at Haydock on standard going and boasts course form that matters here; Daniel Tudhope partners him and he has won on soft with a record suggesting he handles cut in the ground well — a prominent horse who may find the heavy conditions suit if the pace collapses ahead.|
runners_data.comment: Paborus won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing he can compete at this level, but an eighth last time out raises questions, and he carries 131 lb from stall 8 over a trip he has run over before.

runners_data.name: Coppull
runners_data.note: The three-year-old carries the lightest weight at 129lbs for Clive Cox and Hector Crouch, and has won twice over six furlongs including a recent Goodwood win; he is a genuine front-runner who will dispute the lead aggressively, but his age and lack of confirmed heavy-ground experience are legitimate concerns against older, more battle-hardened rivals.|
runners_data.comment: Coppull won last time out and has run over today's trip, giving him solid claims, but his two losses in the three starts before that and a rating of 112 from stall two suggest he sits just below the top echelon here.

races.paceDynamic: Almeraq, Marvelman, and Coppull are all confirmed front-runners in a nine-runner field over six furlongs on heavy ground at Haydock, meaning a fierce pace battle is virtually guaranteed from the off, with no prospect of a tactical crawl. The trio will contest the lead hard through the first two furlongs, creating a punishing early tempo that will drain reserves quickly on ground that is already sapping energy, stretching the field and eliminating any chance of a soft lead. By the three-furlong pole, prominent and midfield runners will be in a position to capitalise as the pace-setters tie each other up, with stamina and the ability to grind through the heavy surface becoming the decisive qualities rather than raw speed or a late kick. This race shape strongly favours a resolute prominent-to-midfield horse with proven heavy-ground ability who can track the carnage without being dragged into it, conserving enough to grind past spent leaders in the final furlong. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; of the redistributed runners, Aramram is a genuine prominent racer who is unlikely to get that berth, while James's Delight — also a prominent type — is shown at hold-up because the prominent slots are oversubscribed, meaning neither can be trusted to race in their optimal shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace war, grinders prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out through the first two furlongs, leaving a true test of stamina from halfway.
scenarios.body: The leaders set a ruinous gallop on heavy ground and capitulate inside the final two furlongs, handing the race to horses who have tracked conservatively and can sustain a gallop to the line; heavy ground stamina is the defining factor here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One leader breaks clear
scenarios.trigger: If Almeraq or Coppull gains an uncontested advantage early after the others fade or miss the break.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner who clears the early melee gets first run on the rail and controls a strong-but-sustainable gallop, keeping enough in reserve to resist the closers on ground that slows late finishes; the winner will have the best blend of speed and stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent stalkers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders tie each other up and a prominent horse tracks just off the pace and swoops in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse settled just behind the leaders avoids the early scrimmage and produces a sustained run from two furlongs out, finding enough on the heavy ground to collar a weakening leader; this shape suits a horse who can race handy without burning energy in the speed duel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late closers finish over them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely destroys the whole prominent group and a hold-up horse picks through a pile of spent rivals.
scenarios.body: A deeper-lying horse threads through weakening rivals in the final furlong as the entire front section collapses under the combination of pace and heavy ground; James's Delight is shown at hold-up through redistribution rather than genuine preference, so this shape carries lower probability.

watchPoints.text: Almeraq, Marvelman, and Coppull are all likely to dispute the lead from the off — watch for a fierce early battle that could burn out all three and leave the race to those tracking just behind.

Paborus has Haydock course form and handles soft ground; watch whether Daniel Tudhope positions him to track the pace battle rather than being dragged into it, as that would give him a significant edge.

Big Mojo with William Buick has the potential to be placed prominently under a smart ride, but his heavy-ground record is near-blank — watch in the paddock for any signs the conditions are against him before taking his market position at face value.

James's Delight and Aramram are both natural prominent horses mapped out of their ideal position due to field congestion — watch whether either manages to slot in closer to the pace than their assessed position suggests, as that would substantially improve their prospects.

The 77-day absence of Kind Of Blue is worth monitoring at the start — a fresh horse can bounce out well or need the run, and on heavy ground a slow early stride could cost him the prominent position he needs to be competitive.

races.name: Betfair Be Friendly Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Poatan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for George Scott with David Egan aboard who needs the pace to collapse in front of him; only two runs at 5f/6f on similar going with no wins and one place, and at 3 years old conceding experience to older rivals on this heavy Haydock turf is a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive thirds two and three starts back show Poatan in consistent form, and he lines up here just 17 days fresh from his latest outing, fit and ready; drawn four carrying 137 lb, he has run over today's trip and looks the most compelling overall profile in the race.

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners this David O'Meara five-year-old who has form on soft but only two wins from 15 soft-or-similar outings and ran just six days ago; a hold-up horse on a flat 5f in heavy ground needs everything to go right, and his 19th-place finish last time is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Toyotomi landed a win three starts back and was third four starts back, showing clear ability at this level, and he arrives fresh on six days' rest carrying 135 lb from stall six with experience over today's trip; the risk is that his last two runs have both disappointed.

runners_data.name: Arklow Lad
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old has three wins on soft from 12 attempts at 5f and wears a tongue-strap; he is a genuine prominent racer and Clifford Lee will be looking to slot cleanly into second or third position behind Jer Batt — 35 days since his last run may mean he returns fresh, which suits heavy conditions.
runners_data.comment: Arklow Lad arrives here on the back of three wins in his last six starts, including a victory two runs back, and he has experience over today's trip; the main concern is that unplaced effort last time out, which he must put behind him.

runners_data.name: Advertised
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's three-year-old with Oliver Stammers in the saddle has a placed effort on soft but runs here on his most testing ground yet; he will look to race prominently and his soft form is encouraging, though inexperience at this trip and going could see him outbattled if the prominent group scrimmages hard early.
runners_data.comment: Advertised has been placed twice in his last five starts, including a second last time out just 15 days ago, and has run over today's trip, making him a serious threat on a rating of 100; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Black Star Boy
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old wears a tongue-strap and Tom Marquand takes the ride; his sole win came on good ground at 5f and his recent efforts show 6th and 0th from six soft outings, meaning the heavy ground looks a likely concern for a horse whose best form has been on a faster surface.
runners_data.comment: Back from a 17-day break and drawn in stall one carrying 130 lb, Black Star Boy has experience over today's trip and a win in his last five starts to his name, though two consecutive unplaced efforts since that success give genuine cause for caution.

runners_data.name: Trilby
runners_data.note: Sam England's six-year-old has won three times on soft from 15 soft-and-similar runs and ran just seven days ago in good form (1st); PJ McDonald is a powerful ally and with a tongue-strap and a pricker, Trilby is arguably the most course-and-distance-proven horse in the prominent group and the one most likely to sustain the effort through the heavy ground.
runners_data.comment: Trilby won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but a fourth two starts back and an unplaced run three starts back temper enthusiasm; carrying 129 lb from stall five, he rates a lively each-way player on a rating of 92.

runners_data.name: Sturlasson
runners_data.note: Stevie Donohoe rides this John Ryan five-year-old who has one win and one place from 15 soft/similar outings; a hold-up racer whose recent form on soft shows a single second place in the past five runs, and the flat Haydock 5f in heavy conditions gives him little time to make his run count from behind.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sturlasson was unplaced most recently and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite the experience over today's distance and going and a return after just 15 days.

runners_data.name: Marching Mac
runners_data.note: Phil McEntee's five-year-old with a tongue-strap and a pricker has strong soft-ground 5f form (2W5P from 15 runs) and Phil McEntee sends out two from six runners — but this horse's instinct is to race up with the pace, and with the prominent slots already crowded he will be pushed wider and later than ideal, which tempers confidence even in a scenario that suits his profile.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of this field on our figures and rated just 85, Marching Mac has managed one win in his last six starts, and a quick turnaround after seven days gives little cause for optimism, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns from stall three.

runners_data.name: Elara May
runners_data.note: Philip McBride's three-year-old is placed twice on soft from 12 similar outings and Hector Crouch rides; her true racing style is to press the pace, but she is competing against too many rivals for those forward positions and will likely find herself in a midfield role she has rarely been asked to fulfil, making her best chance reliant on a chaotic outcome.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and her speed rating gives little encouragement, Elara May does at least bring strong recent fitness having run just six days ago, and she was second last time out — though finding improvement enough to trouble the field from this position looks a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Jer Batt
runners_data.note: David & Nicola Barron's six-year-old ran just yesterday — an extraordinary turnaround — yet his most recent heavy-ground form is a fifth at 5f on this surface and Ray Dawson will allow him to stride on from the gates; as the lone confirmed front-runner he sets the race's tempo and the question is simply whether yesterday's exertion leaves enough in the tank for the final furlong on heavy Haydock turf.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Jer Batt does boast back-to-back thirds three and four starts back, yet a fifth last time out and the burden of 121 lb from stall 10 are the checks on his chance, even if he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 93 suggests he merits respect.

races.paceDynamic: Jer Batt is the sole confirmed front-runner and, critically, goes into this race having run just yesterday — though his record shows he does set out to lead and on heavy ground at Haydock's flat 5f he will bowl along from the gate unchallenged. Behind him, Arklow Lad, Advertised, Black Star Boy, and Trilby all want prominent positions, creating genuine congestion in the first two furlongs that could see bumping and checking 2-3 out in the testing conditions. Marching Mac and Elara May are true prominent-minded horses who are unlikely to secure their preferred berth given the traffic ahead — they will be shuffled into midfield roles that are not their natural homes, blunting their effectiveness. With one relaxed pace-setter and a muddled, jostling bunch behind, the race shape is most likely to produce a straightforward front-running scenario on ground that rewards those who travel economically — hold-up horses will face a difficult task making up ground through deep Haydock going, and the profile that benefits most is the prominent-to-front racer who can tuck in cleanly and pounce on Jer Batt at the furlong pole.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jer Batt Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Jer Batt bowls clear early and dictates a sustainable if testing pace on the heavy ground.
scenarios.body: The prominent pack becomes embroiled in position-fighting behind him, burning energy while Jer Batt conserves his own galloping into the conditions he demonstrated form on at this course; his rivals are too tired from the early jostle to reel him in. Horses who have tracked neatly and avoided the scrimmaging — particularly Trilby and Arklow Lad if they find a clean passage — are best placed to mount the closest challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early position battle forces Jer Batt into an unsustainable gallop and drains the prominent group, leaving a clean-tracking prominent horse to strike at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Trilby's strong record in soft-to-heavy conditions (three wins on soft) and Arklow Lad's proven soft-ground 5f victories give them the class to pick up the pieces if Jer Batt ties up in the final 100 yards. PJ McDonald's strength in a driving finish and Clifford Lee's positional intelligence become decisive factors through testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the field strings out, creating late ground for those held off the pace.
scenarios.body: Toyotomi and Poatan would need an unusually even tempo to allow them to close from off the pace on a flat 5f in heavy ground — conditions that typically reduce the winning margin for closers. Toyotomi's two soft-ground wins in 15 heavy/soft attempts suggest ability, but his recent run just six days ago adds a freshness question.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scramble, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If multiple checks and interference in the prominent cluster open a gap for a runner who finds a clean line on the rail or wide.
scenarios.body: Marching Mac, though mapped to midfield due to redistribution and racing out of role, does carry heavy-ground 5f experience and could profit from carnage if fortune sends him to a gap in the straight. Elara May similarly could capitalise on a scrambled race despite being squeezed from her preferred position, though her soft-ground form shows only placed efforts without a win.

watchPoints.text: Jer Batt's turnaround of just one day between races is extraordinary — watch whether he shows his usual early zip from the gates or if fatigue robs him of the lead before halfway, as the entire race shape depends on him front-running.

The prominent cluster of Arklow Lad, Advertised, Black Star Boy, and Trilby will converge in the first two furlongs — watch for bumping and checking 2-3 out that could compromise the chance of any horse caught in the middle of the pack.

Marching Mac and Elara May are both natural front-pressers forced into unfamiliar midfield positions — if either fights for position and burns energy in the first furlong, they are unlikely to recover on ground this testing.

Trilby ran just seven days ago and returns in excellent form; watch whether PJ McDonald can find a clean passage behind Jer Batt on the rail, as any interference in the prominent pack will cost Trilby more than any other runner given his profile suits this scenario most directly.

Heavy ground at Haydock 5f places a premium on horses who have proven they handle deep going — of the ten runners, only Jer Batt has a recorded run on heavy at this course and distance, making ground suitability the single biggest differentiator to monitor in the early stages.

races.name: HKJC World Pool Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Brian
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who handles soft-side going well (sim-going: 1W3P), and David Egan has strong course familiarity; dropping back from 8f and reverting to 7f suits, though his habit of finishing in mid-pack positions rather than winning raises a question over his ability to produce a winning effort.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and winless in his last five starts, Brian nonetheless holds our top rating among the 12 runners and arrives with distance and going experience to call on; the 86-day absence is the one query, but 140 lb from stall 2 sees him open to respect.

runners_data.name: Star Anthem
runners_data.note: Clive Cox runner who has placed multiple times on soft-ground variants and comes in relatively fresh at 28 days since last run; a true hold-up type who will sit towards the rear of what is an unusually congested back-half of the field, which may restrict his ability to find clean air in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Star Anthem at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and 28 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the worry is that his recent form has been largely disappointing, making a step forward essential from stall one off 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Korker
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish — a serious concern on Heavy ground at Haydock where stamina is at an absolute premium; K.R. Burke's 10-from-39 14-day trainer form gives some stable confidence, but a horse that already fades on faster ground is unlikely to improve on it here.
runners_data.comment: Korker has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 93 ranks him second of these — the main concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, with an eighth most recently.

runners_data.name: Ata Rangi
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field and therefore the pivotal tactical figure; his sim-going record of 8/15 runs with 1W2P on comparable ground is modest, but an uncontested lead in Heavy conditions gives him a structural advantage that raw figures understate — he races very much in role here, which the STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 slightly tempers.
runners_data.comment: Ata Rangi landed a win three starts back but was well beaten last time out, and 42 days off the track plus a stiff 137 lb ask from stall 11 give pause, even if he does hold experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Cape Ashizuri
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's three-year-old is dropping back in trip after a recent 7f effort on Good and has strong form on faster ground (1W1P on Good/GOO); the step up to genuine Heavy is an unknown for this horse, and while his hold-up style means he has everything to prove from off the pace in a congested field, his class at 90 OR is a live threat.
runners_data.comment: Cape Ashizuri won three starts back and was second four starts back, but has been out of the frame in both runs since; he has run over today's trip and returns fit enough on 28 days, though 136 lb is a stern test for a horse ranked mid-field on ratings.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Wilko
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's five-year-old wears a hood and is genuinely a hold-up horse by nature, but with so many closers in this field he is unlikely to secure the deep cover he wants; P.J. McDonald rides and there's a 70-day absence to factor in — the STYLE_FIT note is relevant here because this shape simply does not suit him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 70 days off, Sergeant Wilko does at least have experience over today's trip and a second two starts back shows he can hit the frame, though that eighth last time out is harder to ignore.

runners_data.name: Darkness
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's eight-year-old returns just seven days after his last run, wearing a visor, and has a sim-going record that shows zero wins and zero places from 15 relevant runs — the most damning stat in the field; despite being mapped to midfield, he is a true hold-up horse who will be buried in the pack on current form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Darkness has run over today's trip and returns on a quick seven-day turnaround carrying 135 lb from stall four, though his consistency profile gives little encouragement with a string of sixth-place finishes and unplaced efforts in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Brighton Boy
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old is 14 days fresh and has genuine soft-ground form (1W2P in sim-going), but comes in carrying a 5lb claim with Jake Dickson aboard; a natural closer who will be squeezed for room in the congested hold-up group, he needs a stronger pace than Ata Rangi is likely to set uncontested.
runners_data.comment: Brighton Boy arrives on the back of a third last time out, but has been winless in his last six starts and ranks ninth of twelve on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights off 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Rhoscolyn
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who carries a fade-in-finish flag and wears a tongue-tie — two things that work against survival on punishing Heavy going at Haydock; Daniel Tudhope is a high-quality booking but this horse ran just five days ago, and despite some soft-ground form (1W2P), the finish trend is a real concern in a race where the final furlong will be brutal.
runners_data.comment: Rhoscolyn ran a cracker last time, finishing second just five days ago, and he has experience of today's distance and going; our rating of 90 suggests he holds strong claims, though the quick turnaround after a hard race is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Montezin
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's four-year-old is arguably the most interesting runner in the field — a genuine prominent type who can slot in directly behind Ata Rangi and race in his natural position; his most recent win came over this exact trip on Good, and his tongue-tie/pull combination suggests the yard has put thought into this preparation, making him a strong fit for the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Montezin faces a stiff ask, with his recent form patchy outside a win last time out; he has run over today's trip and returns on a fresh 29-day break, but he looks up against it from stall nine carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's six-year-old wears a hood and comes in 15 days fresh with a sim-going record of 1W2P — decent on paper but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 0/5 offers no confidence; a natural hold-up horse who will find himself further back than ideal in a field where the rear is already crowded with closers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a third two runs back the sole encouragement, Wreck It Ryley faces a stiff task ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh enough 15-day break.

runners_data.name: King Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old returns from 121 days off the track — the longest absence in the field — and while he won over 7f on Soft, the layoff combined with Heavy ground and a field this competitive makes him a big unknown; a true hold-up type mapped to midfield, he would need to bounce back to his best form immediately to factor.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 121 days makes King Of Thunder hard to fancy on a retrieval, and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures he faces a stiff task; he has run over today's trip and the sole win in his last five starts, two runs back, offers a thread of hope.

races.paceDynamic: Ata Rangi is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field over 7f on Heavy ground at Haydock, and with no genuine pressure from rivals capable of matching strides early, Tom Marquand can control tempo from the front without being seriously challenged. On gruelling Heavy ground, that unchallenged lead becomes a significant weapon — a horse allowed to bowl along at a sustainable gallop in these conditions can simply grind the field into submission before they can mount a meaningful challenge. The field behind Ata Rangi is dominated by hold-up horses — Sergeant Wilko, Darkness, Brighton Boy, Rhoscolyn, Wreck It Ryley and King Of Thunder are all true come-from-behind types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many of them to sit where they naturally would — meaning the rear of the field will be unusually congested and the genuine closer's run will be harder to find. This race shape strongly favours the front-running or prominently-raced profile: Ata Rangi controls the pace on its own terms, Montezin can track close, and horses who need a true test to claw back a lead will find the Heavy ground compounds their margin to close.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ata Rangi controls unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ata Rangi leads from the gate and is never seriously pressed, setting a steady-to-fair pace on the Heavy.
scenarios.body: Tom Marquand dictates from the front, controlling fractions on ground that rewards stamina and saps the energy of those making up ground; with no rival capable of matching early, Ata Rangi can conserve enough to hold on up the Haydock straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses close strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the Heavy ground slows the pace sufficiently that closers can launch sustained runs from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A truly testing surface can compress the field if the front-runner backs off the pace, giving the strongest stayers in the hold-up group a fighting chance; Brian and Star Anthem, both genuine Heavy-ground types, would be the most likely beneficiaries in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent pair dominate finish
scenarios.trigger: If Montezin tracks Ata Rangi closely and the two pull clear of a strung-out field in the testing conditions.
scenarios.body: Montezin's recent win at 7f on Good and his prominent racing style make him the most natural companion to Ata Rangi through the race; if Ata Rangi ties up late, Montezin is ideally placed to pounce without having to cover ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise closer pounces late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and a redistributed hold-up horse manages to find clear running and delivers a strong late challenge.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses racing out of their natural role finding space and a path that the congested rear of the field makes unlikely; Cape Ashizuri, stepping up in trip and drawn wide, or King Of Thunder on his first start back from 121 days off, are the most plausible outsider beneficiaries if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Ata Rangi's early position is critical — if Montezin pushes up to track closely, watch whether Tom Marquand quickens or backs off, as the pace set in the first two furlongs will define whether closers can get back into it.

The rear of the field — Sergeant Wilko, Darkness, Rhoscolyn, Brighton Boy, Wreck It Ryley and King Of Thunder — will all be fighting for the same ground with true hold-up instincts; watch for traffic trouble and blocked runs entering the Haydock straight, which could be decisive.

Rhoscolyn and Korker both carry fade-in-finish flags, and on Heavy ground a horse that already fades can stop very suddenly — jockeys behind them should be alert to these horses dropping away sharply from two furlongs out.
Cape Ashizuri has never raced on going as testing as Heavy; watch the market moves and paddock demeanour before the off to gauge confidence from the Quinn yard that he handles the conditions.

Darkness runs just seven days after his last outing — monitor for any signs of fatigue or below-par going to post, as the David O'Meara yard has a busy book and a quick return on a horse with zero sim-going wins is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Yanifer
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Yanifer nonetheless tops our ratings, if only narrowly, and having run over today's trip and conditions before, he arrives fit on a 14-day turnaround carrying 140 lb from stall four — the fourth placing two starts back is his best recent showing.

runners_data.name: Metal Merchant
runners_data.comment: Metal Merchant shaped with some promise when fourth two starts back, and with experience over today's trip and going he retains claims at a mark of 82 — though he is winless in his last five starts and that ninth last time out is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Final Night
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Final Night has been runner-up three times in recent form without converting, and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip before and 24 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.comment: Military Leader won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims, but carrying 137 lb from stall 8 and ranked fifth of twelve in the field suggests he faces a stiff enough task to justify a midfield projection.

runners_data.name: Caim
runners_data.comment: Caim shaped with plenty of promise when finishing second three starts back and a winner four starts back, and she returns here on a quick 16-day turnaround with experience over today's trip; the 137 lb burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Miletus
runners_data.comment: Miletus won three starts back and was third four starts back, showing he has the ability to mix it in these grades, but back-to-back fifths since suggest he is struggling to recapture that form; has run over today's trip and returns after 36 days off carrying 136 lb from stall ten.

runners_data.name: Jungle Ruler
runners_data.comment: Jungle Ruler has been a model of consistency, finishing in the top five in each of his last six starts with a second last time out and a third two starts back, and his experience over today's trip bolsters his claims at a useful 94 on our rating; the chief concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Crown Office
runners_data.comment: Crown Office has found the first three three times in his last five starts, and his speed figure of 79 sits well below the level required here, making him hard to fancy ranked ninth of twelve; he does carry a light weight from stall one and has run over today's trip, which are slim consolations.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Monoceros does at least return here with distance experience and 38 days of freshness, though a pulled-up run among recent efforts and a mark of 81 give cause for caution from stall three.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, The Sweet Escape faces a stiff ask against this field, yet his recent form is genuinely eye-catching: a winner last time out and winners three and four starts back, with a runner-up finish two starts back adding consistency, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Bearin Up
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Bearin Up arrives on the back of an unplaced effort and faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and two wins in her last six starts show she is capable of better.

runners_data.name: Kindest Nation
runners_data.comment: Kindest Nation shaped with promise when third last time out, and her distance and going experience are in her favour, but she has been winless in her last five starts and her rating of 83 suggests she faces a stiff task from stall nine carrying 127 lb.
